lines.text: The writer instructs the listener so that his trust may be in the LORD, and he has written thirty sayings.
Do not rob a poor man or crush the afflicted at the gate, for the king will take up their case.
Do not put up security for debts, or your bed may be taken from under you.
A man skilled in his work will be stationed in the presence of priests, not before obscure men.
Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless, for their Redeemer is strong.
